issues.legal_issue: An appellate judgment that allows an appeal and sets aside the challenged judgment displaces the lower-court judgment and determines the operative disposition of the underlying proceedings.
material_facts: The Supreme Court had granted leave and allowed appeals against earlier High Court judgments concerning the same land and parties.
The formal decree set aside both the High Court judgments and the single-judge orders, and substituted an order dismissing the underlying writ petitions.
The prior Supreme Court judgment did not remand the matter or preserve the High Court findings.
issues.conclusion: The earlier High Court judgments were set aside in their entirety, the underlying writ petitions stood dismissed, and the proceedings challenged in those petitions were not left open for renewed challenge.
issues.legal_principle: Once leave to appeal is granted and the appeal is decided, the appellate judgment attracts the doctrine of merger, whether it reverses, modifies, or affirms the judgment below; the lower judgment ceases to operate except to the extent expressly preserved. The Court relied on Kunhayammed v. State of Kerala (2000) 6 SCC 359, Gojer Bros. (P) Ltd. v. Ratan Lal Singh (1974) 2 SCC 453, and Dharam Dutt v. Union of India (2004) 1 SCC 712. It also held that a final Supreme Court judgment cannot be collaterally challenged on the ground that an issue or argument was not considered, relying on Kausalya Devi Bogra v. Land Acquisition Officer (1984) 2 SCC 324, Ballabhdas Mathurdas Lakhani v. Municipal Committee, Malkapur (1970) 2 SCC 267, Kesho Ram and Co. v. Union of India (1989) 3 SCC 151, Director of Settlements, A.P. v. M.R. Apparao (2002) 4 SCC 638, Anil Kumar Neotia v. Union of India (1988) 2 SCC 587, Palitana Sugar Mills (P) Ltd. v. State of Gujarat (2004) 12 SCC 645, and A.V. Papayya Sastry v. Government of A.P. (2007) 4 SCC 221.

rule.if: appeal_from_writ_judgment and supreme_court_granted_leave and supreme_court_allowed_appeal and (no_remand_order or no_lower_court_finding_preserved)

predicates.appeal_from_writ_judgment: A party pursued an appeal against a judgment deciding writ proceedings.
predicates.supreme_court_granted_leave: The Supreme Court granted leave to appeal and exercised appellate jurisdiction.
predicates.supreme_court_allowed_appeal: The Supreme Court allowed the appeal against the challenged judgment.
predicates.no_remand_order: The Supreme Court did not remit the matter for further adjudication.
predicates.no_lower_court_finding_preserved: The Supreme Court did not expressly preserve any finding or part of the lower-court judgment.

issues.definition: When an appeal from a writ judgment is allowed after leave, and the matter is neither remanded nor any lower-court finding preserved, the prior judgment is set aside and the underlying petitions are dismissed.

issues.legal_issue: A landholder who represented land as vacant in declarations, relied on those declarations to obtain the release of other land, and allowed the resulting surplus determination to become final cannot later reopen that determination by claiming the declarations were mistaken.
material_facts: The landholders described the land as grazing or vacant land in declarations and invoked the urban land ceiling process.

They relied on the urban land declarations in seeking the release of land previously declared surplus under agricultural land reform proceedings; the land was returned to them after that application succeeded.
The land was within an urban agglomeration, and a housing society had obtained approval for a residential layout before the declarations were filed.
The surplus determination and subsequent proceedings were not challenged by the landholders through the available statutory process, and the declarations were not withdrawn.
The landholders sought fresh consideration many years after the declarations and the completion of the ceiling proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The landholders and those claiming through them were bound by the declarations and the final surplus determination and could not reopen the proceedings on the ground that the declarations had been made under a mistaken impression.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 2(o) and 2(q) of the Urban Land (Ceiling and Regulation) Act, 1976 define urban land and vacant land; under Section 6(1) and its Explanation, the relevant date depends on when land becomes vacant land. A later master plan may be considered where land becomes vacant land after the Act commenced, as held in State of Andhra Pradesh v. N. Audikesava Reddy (2002) 1 SCC 227, which overruled Atia Mohammadi Begum v. State of U.P. (1993) 2 SCC 546 to that extent. Here the land was vacant when the declarations were made, and the later extension of the master plan did not undermine them. The Court also applied the principle that a party cannot approbate and reprobate by relying on a transaction and later disavowing it, and the principles of constructive res judicata under Section 11 and Explanation IV of the Code of Civil Procedure, as applied to writ proceedings in Forward Construction Co. v. Prabhat Mandal (Regd.), Andheri (1986) 1 SCC 100 and Ishwar Dutt v. Land Acquisition Collector (2005) 7 SCC 190.

rule.if: appeal_from_writ_dismissal and landholders_declared_land_vacant and landholders_relied_on_declarations_for_benefit and surplus_determination_not_challenged and declarations_not_withdrawn

predicates.appeal_from_writ_dismissal: The matter is an appeal arising from the dismissal of writ proceedings challenging land-ceiling proceedings.
predicates.landholders_declared_land_vacant: The landholders described the land as vacant or non-agricultural in declarations to the competent authority.
predicates.landholders_relied_on_declarations_for_b: The landholders relied on those declarations to obtain a benefit concerning their land in another proceeding.
predicates.surplus_determination_not_challenged: The landholders did not use the available process to challenge the resulting surplus determination and subsequent proceedings.
predicates.declarations_not_withdrawn: The landholders did not withdraw the declarations on which the determination was based.

issues.definition: If landholders in an appeal arising from dismissed writ proceedings declared the land vacant, relied on that declaration for a benefit, left the surplus determination unchallenged, and did not withdraw their declarations, the determination remains final and cannot be reopened.

issues.legal_issue: A claimant who is not in possession of surplus land when the applicable policy requires possession, and whose land has already been allotted to public authorities, is not entitled to the claimed exemption or regularization benefit.
material_facts: The land had been allotted to a public development authority before the claimants sought the exemption benefit.
The claimants were not in possession of the land at the relevant time, and the land was subsequently allotted to an industrial infrastructure corporation.
The exemption policy applied where the declarant remained in possession until the specified cutoff and the Government took possession after that cutoff.
The regularization policies made occupation or possession a prerequisite to allotment of surplus land.
issues.conclusion: The claimants were not entitled to the claimed exemption or regularization benefits.
issues.legal_principle: The Court construed the applicable government orders as requiring the declarant to have remained in possession up to the relevant cutoff for the exemption benefit, and construed the regularization orders as requiring occupation or possession as a condition of allotment. It also applied the rule that land vested in the State free from encumbrances is owned by the State and the former owner has no continuing right to it, relying on Smt. Sulochana Chandrakant Galande v. Pune Municipal Transport (2010) 7 SCALE 571.

rule.if: appeal_from_writ_dismissal and claimants_lacked_possession_at_relevant_cutoff and land_already_allotted_to_public_authority and (exemption_requires_continuing_possession or regularization_requires_occupation)

predicates.appeal_from_writ_dismissal: The matter is an appeal arising from the dismissal of writ proceedings challenging the treatment or allotment of surplus land.
predicates.claimants_lacked_possession_at_relevant_: The claimants were not in possession of the land at the time by which the applicable policy required them to remain in possession.
predicates.land_already_allotted_to_public_authorit: The land had already been allotted to a public authority before the claimants sought the benefit.
predicates.exemption_requires_continuing_possession: The exemption policy makes continued possession until a specified cutoff a condition of eligibility.
predicates.regularization_requires_occupation: The regularization policy makes occupation or possession a condition of eligibility for allotment.

issues.definition: In an appeal arising from dismissed writ proceedings, claimants who lacked possession at the relevant cutoff and whose land was already allotted to a public authority are not entitled to a benefit that requires continued possession or occupation.

issues.legal_issue: Possession of a large tract of land may be taken through a properly executed panchnama when the taking is documented and the panchnama is not challenged.
material_facts: The State asserted that it took possession of the surplus land through a panchnama signed by witnesses.
The owners were not in possession when the State asserted that possession was taken.
The appellants did not challenge the panchnama in any proceeding.
The land comprised a large tract.
issues.conclusion: The State had legally and validly taken possession through the panchnama.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that possession of a large tract may be taken by a properly executed panchnama, relying on Sita Ram Bhandar Society, New Delhi v. Lieutenant Governor, Government of NCT of Delhi (2009) 10 SCC 501. It upheld the finding that possession had been taken where the panchnama was signed by witnesses and had not been challenged.

rule.if: appeal_from_writ_dismissal and large_tract_of_land and possession_documented_by_panchnama and panchnama_signed_by_witnesses and panchnama_not_challenged

predicates.appeal_from_writ_dismissal: The matter is an appeal arising from the dismissal of writ proceedings that challenge the State's taking of possession.
predicates.large_tract_of_land: The land from which possession was taken comprises a large tract.
predicates.possession_documented_by_panchnama: The State recorded the taking of possession in a panchnama.
predicates.panchnama_signed_by_witnesses: Witnesses signed the panchnama recording the taking of possession.
predicates.panchnama_not_challenged: The affected parties did not challenge the panchnama in any proceeding.

issues.definition: In an appeal challenging the taking of possession, a properly documented and witnessed panchnama that has not been challenged establishes valid possession-taking of a large tract.
